commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly. A zone identifier, when present, is part of the
comparison so link-local literals on different zones do not match.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: The overflow exists only when the two edits are combined. 9205b35 extends knownhost_parse_ipv6 so a successful parse writes the 16-byte IPv6 address and, if the literal carries an RFC 4007 zone id, the zone text and a NUL immediately after it. That commit also sizes the only caller it has (knownhost_plain_match) to KNOWNHOST_IPV6_BINLEN and rejects a longer zone, so the extra bytes stay in range. e43754b adds a readline check that a '%' is a real IPv6 zone id. It allocates 16 bytes, which is the historical result[16] address and exactly what the unmodified parser stores, then calls knownhost_parse_ipv6. On the original parser a zoned name fails before any byte past that allocation is written; on the widened parser fe80::1%eth0 succeeds and the zone memcpy runs past the 16-byte heap block (heap-buffer-overflow under ASan). Applying either edit alone does not fire: without the zone tail the 16-byte buffer is sufficient, and without the new caller the tail is only written into the BINLEN buffer from 9205b35. The two diffs disagree about the helper's output size, and that disagreement is not visible inside either diff. Undoing one commit stops the crash only by dropping that commit's maintenance (zone-aware comparison, or the '%' check). A fix that keeps both has to line the readline allocation up with the output length introduced in 9205b35; the faulty size is the relationship between the commits, not a self-contained mistake in one of them.
